name: Sankarism
summary: Sankarism is the programme of Thomas Sankara's 1983-87 revolution in Burkina Faso: a self-described democratic and popular, anti-imperialist revolution that smashed the neocolonial state, mobilised the people through Committees for the Defence of the Revolution, and sought a planned, self-sufficient economy free of foreign debt and aid. It put women's emancipation, health, literacy and reforestation at the centre, and combined pan-African non-alignment with austere, anti-corruption leadership. In power it also dissolved old parties, set up revolutionary tribunals and crushed a teachers' strike.
scope: The doctrine and record of Sankara's National Council of the Revolution (1983-1987): the Political Orientation Speech, his speeches on women, debt, ecology and the UN, and the regime's documented acts. Later parties that use the label (which split over Marxism) and recent leaders compared to Sankara are excluded.

notes: Positions rest on Sankara's speeches and the regime's documented record (parties dissolved, tribunals, 1985 teachers' strike, land nationalisation); where a record exists it answers instead of the speeches. Themes searched with no recorded position: religion and church-state relations, criminal justice beyond tribunals, immigration, sexuality, drugs, technology policy, taxation of wealth, media regulation, electoral design, central banking. The Pathfinder anthology and journal articles were unavailable, so the record rests on the speeches available online plus two dissertations and one review. Contemporary Sankarist parties differ on Marxism, so no single party platform is used.
